title: Fibre degree bounds hold for all field-valued points (Stacks 03J5)
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $n\ge0$ an integer. The following are equivalent: (1) $n$ bounds the degrees of the fibres of $f$ [def-weil-pbc-fibre-degree-bound]; (2) for every field $K$ and every morphism of schemes $\operatorname{Spec}K\to Y$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the fibre product $X_K=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-pc-fibre-product], regarded as a scheme over $K$ through its second projection $X_K\to\operatorname{Spec}K$, is finite over $K$ (the projection is a finite morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]) and $\dim_K\Gamma(X_K,\mathcal O_{X_K})\le n$, where $\Gamma(X_K,\mathcal O_{X_K})$ is a $K$-algebra through the ring map induced by the projection.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 03J5 (lemma-characterize-universally-bounded), line 15322, equivalence of (1) and (2), and the first two sentences of its proof ((2)=>(1) trivial, taking Spec kappa(y) -> Y; (1)=>(2) since X_K = Spec K x_{Spec kappa(y)} X_y for y the image of Spec K -> Y)

mathlib_searches.query: base change of scheme finite over residue field to a field extension, finrank of global sections preserved
mathlib_searches.verdict: no match (Module.finrank_baseChange is the linear-algebra ingredient of (1)=>(2); no scheme statement)

mathlib_searches.query: for every morphism Spec K -> Y from a field, the fibre product X x_Y Spec K is finite over K of degree at most n

mathlib_searches.verdict: no match: Scheme.Hom.finrank is the rank of a finite flat morphism; Mathlib has no notion of bounded fibre degrees
